To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the life history traits of the upland bully varied among populations but were not related to either water temperature or average parasite load in the populations.

(i) life history traits of upland bully varied between populations; (ii) there was no evidence that life history traits were related to either temperature or parasite load, and (iii) there were trade-offs between egg size, egg number and offspring size, which varied among populations.

(1) life history traits can vary between populations of the same species, (2) life history traits are not necessarily linked to environmental factors such as water temperature and parasite load, (3) life history traits vary among populations of a species even though they are exposed to the same environmental factors, and (4) life history traits may be linked to environmental factors in some populations of a species, but not in others.

the effects of parasitic infection, temperature and life history on the ecology of freshwater fish.
how the life history traits of freshwater fishes vary among populations, and the extent to which this variation is associated with differences in environmental conditions.
how parasites affect life history evolution and population dynamics in natural host populations.
